Give the reason. For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules: 1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting. 2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 13 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply. 3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected. 4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain". 5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string. 6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one. 7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol. 8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved. 9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only. 10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later). 11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null. Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: Link no longer expects a nested <a> child
paths.description: In Next.js 13, <Link> always renders <a> itself and forwards props to it. Code written for Next.js 12 that nests a manual <a> inside <Link> follows the old pattern and needs migration. The text says the nested <a> is no longer required, and a codemod is provided to upgrade links.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 13, where <Link> always renders <a> by default.
quotes: In Next.js 13, <Link> always renders <a> and allows you to forward props to the underlying tag.
conditions.relevance: Ties the behavior change to release 13, which a 12 -> 14 upgrade crosses.

conditions.statement: The application uses the <Link> component imported from next/link.
conditions.relevance: The change affects the <Link> component from next/link.

conditions.statement: The application nests a manual <a> tag as a child of <Link>, the Next.js 12 pattern.
quotes: <a> has to be nested otherwise it's excluded
conditions.relevance: This is the Next.js 12 pattern that is no longer required in 13 and that the new-link codemod upgrades.
ambiguities: The text does not state what happens in Next.js 13 when a nested <a> remains inside <Link>, only that it is no longer required.

conditions.statement: The application already enabled the experimental <Link> behavior added in 12.2 and has no nested <a> children.
quotes: This behavior was added as an experimental option in version 12.2 and is now the default.
conditions.relevance: Applications that already adopted the experimental option may have little or no migration work.
ambiguities: The text does not name the experimental option or state its effect on apps that enabled it.

suggested_actions: Run the new-link codemod to upgrade links to Next.js 13.
Remove the nested <a> child from <Link> components and put the link text or content directly inside <Link>.
Pass props that were previously set on the nested <a> directly to <Link>, which forwards them to the underlying <a>.
